messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT triggered: kv_cache_eviction_rate > 5% (5m avg) on pool=default in us-west-2. Pager: eng-oncall. Incident bot ID: INC-1938001111

aaron: acked — I'm oncall. tagging: @maria @kevin. any customer-facing errors yet?

maria: looking at traces now. I see a spike in eviction rate starting 09:12 UTC, correlates with a batch job hitting large prefixes. latency p50 unaffected but p95 up ~120ms on inference route. no 5xxs yet.

kevin: adding logs: `kv_cache.evictions_total` jumped from ~20/min to ~450/min for the default pool. access_rate steady. looks like TTL churn not access pattern.

jun: checking autoscaler / pod churn — no restarts. memory pressure on kv-cache pods is near limit. might be eviction due to OOM pressure from a different container on the node.

maria: pulling node metrics. three nodes in that AZ show memory spike at 09:11. candidate culprit: batch-transform job `model-batch-ingest-27`. ops-scout-bot shows scheduled cron at 09:10.

cassie: pinging CS — any customer reports? none yet. but we should go into mitigation to avoid errors.

aaron: mitigation plan: 1) throttle the batch job (pause), 2) increase kv-cache memory limit on pool pods as temporary hotfix, 3) silence noisy pages until we confirm impact window. I'll take 1 and 2.

aaron: `kubectl scale job model-batch-ingest-27 --replicas=0 -n batch-jobs` — paused the job.

aaron: increasing kv-cache memory limit on one replacement pod to test:
```
kubectl patch statefulset kv-cache -n inference --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kv-cache","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"8Gi"},"requests":{"memory":"8Gi"}}}]}}}}'
```

maria: applied to one pod, rolling restart triggered. eviction rate dropped to ~0.9% in 2 mins. p95 latency returned to baseline. good sign.

oncall-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied by aaron and maria. Current status: partial mitigation, monitoring.

kevin: root cause hypothesis: batch job created huge ephemeral prefixes that consumed cache memory and triggered eviction cascade. alerts are firing for transient spikes — alert rule fires on short windows.

maria: agreed. we should avoid paging on short single-window spikes. proposal: require sustained >5% for 10m AND group by model_pool so paging only when severity is broad. also add a per-customer amplification check so we page immediately if top-10 customer hit-rate drops.

jun: +1. also, create a dashboard tile showing eviction heatmap by prefix, and a timeline widget that overlays `kv_cache.hitrate` and `kv_cache.eviction_rate` with autoscale events.

cassie: customer-impact note: no active 5xxs or escalations, but heavy customers might see slight latency increases. I told CS to monitor for complaints and we prepped a short playbook to reply.

aaron: handing off to @kevin — I need to jump to a different pager. kevin, if you accept please own follow-ups and post a summary.

kevin: I accept handoff at 09:22 UTC. next steps: 1) revert the memory patch to config-managed value after we prepare a proper capacity increase, 2) schedule an oncall postmortem, 3) implement alert tuning PR.

kevin: temporary alert change — added an alertmanager silence for the current incidents window to avoid duplicates: `amtool silence add --starts 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z --ends 2026-03-15T10:00:00Z "kv_cache_eviction_rate - incident 1938001111"`

sre-runbook-bot: runbook lookup: `kv-cache-high-eviction` runbook suggests: check OOMs -> inspect recent cron jobs -> throttle heavy tail jobs -> increase cache capacity or tune TTLs.

kevin: creating follow-up tickets now: TICKET-ENG-2345 (dashboard + alert change), TICKET-OPS-2346 (capacity sizing for kv-cache), TICKET-PS-2347 (customer impact + CS message template).

maria: for the alert rule, suggested PromQL:```
(evictions_total[10m] / max(1, accesses_total[10m])) * 100 > 5
and increase duration to 10m
group_left(model_pool)
```

kevin: will include both sustained window and group_by in PR. also add a suppression for transient single-minute spikes: alert only fires if `increase(evictions_total[5m]) > 100` AND sustained >5% for 10m.

cassie: post-incident customer checklist: 1) proactively notify top-10 customers using batch-ids that touched the prefixed keys, 2) offer a brief explanation and reassure retry behavior is respected. CS will draft.

kevin: summary (handed-off): incident caused by an internal batch job creating memory pressure -> kv-cache evictions -> p95 latency blip. mitigated by pausing job and bumping cache memory. Next actions: dashboard tile, alert tuning PR (sustain + group_by + customer amplifiers), capacity sizing, oncall postmortem.

kevin: closing incident thread. I'll update the incident tracker with final timeline and attach graphs. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
